chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who emancipated a man, for whom is his guardianship and for whom is his inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: For the one who emancipated him, except if there happen to be for him an inheritor other than her.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a slave freed by a woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a woman’s emancipation of a male slave grants her both walayah (guardianship) and mirath (inheritance), mirroring the rights of a male emancipator, unless a competing heir exists. This ruling underscores the legal agency of women in the Shia tradition, affirming that emancipation creates a direct kinship bond (mawla) independent of gender, thereby integrating women into the broader framework of Islamic inheritance and guardianship law.
